questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: My boyfriend is from Poland, and I went to Poland with him the summer before my Erasmus. I really like the polish culture, and thought it was interesting to stay in a Central European country. It learned me new perspectives, and expanded my horizon. I think it helped me get a bigger understand of the importance of EU and the different conflicts in Europe.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Warsaw University was really helpful providing information about my stay, and we had several online meetings before. Both my mobility coordinators in Denmark and Poland was quick to answer and a big help. If I had any questions I quickly got an answer and help, so I found it easy finding the information I needed before arrival. The only difficulties was the Erasmus proces with OLA etc. which took a long time and was difficult.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had a wonderful mobility coordinator who was available 24 hours always responding and helping us. I also had a "Buddy/mentor", who is a polish friend we can apply for to help us doing our stay. My mentor ended up being one of best friends at my stay and biggest supporters, she helped me if I had any questions and was a big help. I felt like we had a lot of assistance, and Warsaw university has a 2 week long intro week, and many WhatsApp groups that can help.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult to find housing, and one of my biggest struggles. I found recommendation on Pepehousing, where I could get a discount (from Warsaw university). I had to pay deposit before signing contract, and sign contract before seeing apartment. So it felt a bit sketchy, but in the end the apartment looked like the pictures and it worked out. The cons about the apartment was that it was really dirty when we moved in and the owners wouldn't take responsibility (I rented from housemates, and would not recommend, since the apartment can be dirty with a lack of communication). Some of my friends stayed at a dorm, but many of the dorms were in horrible shape but very cheap. The worst dormitories will also be removed in the future, since Warsaw university didn't know about dorm.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can be really hard to find a place, would recommend asking university for help or former students. It can be hard (and expensive) but not impossible to find a place. I also stayed with my boyfriend and wanted a studio apartment, which made it more difficult. I think Pepe housing I used was more expensive than it should be, but for me it was worth it, since it can be hard to navigate.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The university is good at helping, and will take feedback serious about dormitories

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Registration is pretty late, and near semester start. But it was okay since you can be pretty sure to get all of the courses you want, and they inform well about the registration process. We register at their website for Erasmus courses, and write to the professors by mail if we want to take regular courses. I got all of the courses I wanted, even though half of mine was regular courses

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The mobility coordinator was good at helping, and we also had online meetings before about how to register

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 100% succesfull

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be sure about the schedule and that the classes is not at the same time. It is a long process, especially with OLA, but it work out in the end. There is good options to cancel classes if regretted, and the professors almost never says no to take extra students, if there is not enough spaces on the website.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was fine, but very different from my home university

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Very different, some of my classes had good professors that made the course interesting, others seemed a bit unprepared. So very mixed.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It´s more similar to high school in Denmark since the classes is mandatory, include activity and presentations in your grade. Students is very involved in the teaching, and there is a lot of the exams that is multiple choice. Most of the exams is written by hand.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
2025Z Comparative Political Systems (I) 2102-ANG-L-D3CPSY Groups for course
Seminar Comparative Political Systems (I)
- it was okay, but not as good as the rest I recommend. The professor was really sweet, but too much of the class was student presentations


2025Z European Primary and Secondary Law 2105-EPE-L-D3EPSL Groups for course
Seminar European Primary and Secondary Law
- My favourite course. Really well structured and a good professor. Not any student presentations, which I liked, so only the professor taught this class. There was student preparation for every class, making it structured. Really liked this class. 

2025Z Poland's Foreign Policy 2100-ERASMUS-PFPO Groups for course
Seminar Poland's Foreign Policy
- Half student presentations half professors presentation. Liked the professor and my class.

2025Z The Central and East European Perspective on Russia 2100-ERASMUS-CEUE Groups for course
Seminar The Central and East European Perspective on Russia
- Liked the professor, and he was a good teacher. Half student presentation and professors presentation, so kind of similar structure as Polands foreign policy class

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
I travel a lot and haven't included that. But I think with the Erasmus grant and SU it was easy to afford Poland. I travelled through most of Poland.

My unexpected cost was moving in. You can't expect a functional kitchen, so need to buy most of the kitchen supplies.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Prices in average half price of Denmark (groceries etc). But housing was pretty expensive if not staying in a dormitory. Prices as expected since I visited Poland before, but if you don't know Poland is more expensive that expected (still not expensive compared to Denmark).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You can take language classes and sport classes at universiy

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kind of activities: museum trips, parties, social events, language courses, events for seeing the city etc. I think everything imaginable is available, really good offers

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to movie nights (didn't do myself but seemed nice), heard good about international dinner, taking polish intensive course, just meet with people especially in the beginning, many went to multipub every wednesday. My biggest recommendation is to get a polish mentor

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
My favourite places (in ranked priority) in Poland:
- Zakopane for hiking
- Gdańsk (see the city, Second World War museum)
- Wroclaw
- Kraków (see the saltmine, castle and Auschwitz)
- Malbork (to see the castle, near Gdansk so trip can be combined but I did it in a one-day trip)
- Poznan
- Lublin
- Bialystok (national park)
- Lodz

In Warsaw:
- Wilanow palace
- POLIN museum
- Uprising museum
- Royal castle
- Botanical garden

Restaurants:
- Nabank (brunch)
- No. 34 coffee and breakfast
- Bar Rascal 
- Tikhari modern Georgia
- Same Krafty (beer)
- Księgarnia Wrzenie Świata (Café to study - silent żonę)
- and many other places, so many good food places!!!

-

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think it was pretty easy to adjust to the local culture, but as a dane you need to get used to having a really formal reaction to the professors.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Get a polish friend, not be shy to ask people If there want to hang out (everyone just want to get to know other people and get friends)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not many, only the things with the professors described before

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The history and the polish people is very proud

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Explore Poland
- Be open and don't be afraid to ask people if they want to do anything with you
- Dont stress about studying but enjoy the experience and value your time there

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that I can think of

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All of the people I met and getting to know more about Poland and its history and people

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: When my Erasmus ended and saying goodbye to all of the people I met

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Really recommend to go, the best months of my life

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
